description: AI Village presentations from DEF CON 26 covering machine learning security, AI safety, adversarial techniques, and ethical considerations in artificial intelligence.

talks.title: Identifying and Correlating Anomalies in Internetwide Scan
talks.teaser: Identifying and correlating anomalies in internet-wide network scan data using machine learning.
talks.summary:
Network Scanning Scale

Internet-wide scanning generates massive datasets. Identifying meaningful anomalies in this data is challenging without machine learning approaches.

Anomaly Detection

The presentation covers techniques for identifying anomalies in scan data and correlating them across scans. Understanding patterns in global internet scans reveals infrastructure vulnerabilities.

Machine Learning Application

ML models trained on network scan data can identify unusual patterns, misconfigurations, and potentially vulnerable systems at scale.

Applications

Identifying anomalies in internet-wide scans enables discovery of vulnerable services and infrastructure before attackers do.

talks.title: Chatting with Your Programs to Find Vulnerabilities
talks.teaser: Using natural language interaction with ML to discover vulnerabilities in software programs.
talks.summary:
AI-Assisted Vulnerability Discovery

Natural language processing enables new approaches to vulnerability discovery. Instead of traditional code analysis, conversational interfaces guide the discovery process.

Chatbot Approach

The technique uses chatbots to interact with programs and analyze responses for vulnerability indicators. This approach simplifies complex vulnerability discovery processes.

Program Analysis

Chatting with programs through AI interfaces reveals vulnerabilities through interactive analysis rather than static or dynamic testing alone.

Application

Natural language-driven vulnerability discovery offers new possibilities for security testing and vulnerability identification.

talks.title: Generating Labeled Data From Adversary Sims with MITRE ATT&CK
talks.teaser: Generating labeled datasets from adversary simulations using MITRE ATT&CK framework for ML training.
talks.summary:
Labeled Data Challenge

Machine learning for security requires labeled datasets. Generating realistic labeled data for adversarial scenarios is difficult.

MITRE ATT&CK Integration

Using MITRE ATT&CK framework to simulate adversary behaviors generates labeled data for training ML models. Each simulated attack provides labeled examples.

Adversary Simulation

Running adversary simulations with known attack techniques from MITRE ATT&CK generates training data with accurate labels.

Model Training

Labeled data from adversary simulations enables training ML models to detect attack techniques and adversary behaviors in real environments.

talks.title: Responsible Offensive Machine Learning
talks.teaser: Panel discussion on responsible and ethical approaches to offensive machine learning research.
talks.summary:
Ethical Challenges

Offensive machine learning raises ethical and safety concerns. Researchers must balance innovation with responsibility.

Responsible Disclosure

Finding vulnerabilities in ML systems requires responsible approaches to disclosure and mitigation. Publishing exploits without vendor coordination causes harm.

AI Safety Considerations

Offensive ML research intersects with AI safety. Weaponizing AI requires careful ethical consideration and oversight.

Panel Discussion

The panel covers ethical frameworks for offensive ML, responsible vulnerability disclosure, and balancing innovation with safety in AI security research.

talks.title: The Great Power of AI Algorithmic Mirrors of Society
talks.teaser: Examining how AI systems and algorithms can mirror societal biases and their security implications.
talks.summary:
Algorithmic Bias

AI systems trained on historical data perpetuate and amplify societal biases. These algorithmic mirrors reflect discrimination present in training data.

Second-Order Effects

Bias in AI systems has security and safety implications. Biased ML models in security contexts create exploitable disparities.

Social Impact

AI systems that discriminate against protected groups cause real-world harm. The security community must understand and address these issues.

Mitigation Approaches

Detecting and mitigating bias requires understanding how training data and model architectures perpetuate discrimination. Security researchers must consider fairness in ML systems.

talks.title: Machine Learning Model Hardening For Fun and Profit
talks.teaser: Techniques for hardening machine learning models against adversarial attacks and evasion.
talks.summary:
Model Vulnerability

Machine learning models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that cause misclassification. Hardening models improves robustness against attacks.

Adversarial Training

Training models on adversarial examples improves resistance to attacks. Exposing models to attacks during training builds robustness.

Evasion Resistance

Hardened models resist evasion attempts by adversaries. Techniques include adversarial training, input validation, and defensive distillation.

Practical Hardening

The presentation covers practical methods for hardening ML models in security applications. Model hardening makes systems more resistant to attacks and manipulation.
